correctness.rationale: Uniqueness forces the optimizer to inherit O(n-1) symmetry, reducing it to center c e_1 and semiaxes (a,b,...,b). Slab and cone containment are converted exactly into a<=min(s,1-s) and b^2<=((n+s)^2-a^2)/(n^2-1). Volume is strictly increasing in a up to the slab cap; the resulting s-branch is strictly increasing before s=1/2 and strictly decreasing after it. This uniquely yields c=-1/2, a=1/2, b^2=n/(n-1). The source independently supplies J(K_n)=B_2^n and feasibility of the same ellipsoid.

value.rationale: The recent proof uses this cone family as the sharpness witness but only needs a feasible ellipsoid and explicitly avoids a maximality claim. Determining the exact John ellipsoid converts its asymptotic witness into a precise finite-dimensional benchmark, while the source states that fixed-dimensional best constants remain open.
